stories.headline: Canada reaches NATO 2% defense spending target, announces $3B for Maritime provinces
stories.summary: For the first time since 1990, Canada has met NATO's 2% GDP defense spending target. Prime Minister Carney announced over $3 billion in new defense infrastructure spending for Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, with $2+ billion for Nova Scotia alone to modernize CFB Halifax and build facilities for new warships and aircraft.

stories.headline: Pierre Poilievre appears on Joe Rogan podcast, sparks debate over misinformation claims
stories.summary: Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre sat for a lengthy interview on The Joe Rogan Experience podcast, reaching an estimated 20+ million viewers. The appearance generated fact-checking from critics who accused him of spreading misinformation on immigration numbers and other topics, while supporters praised his international outreach.

stories.headline: Air Canada CEO faces backlash for English-only condolences after fatal LaGuardia crash
stories.summary: Air Canada CEO Michael Rousseau delivered condolences exclusively in English following a deadly plane crash at LaGuardia Airport that killed two pilots, including French-Canadian Antoine Forest. Prime Minister Carney, Quebec Premier Legault, and Bloc Québécois leaders called his response lacking in judgment and compassion, with some demanding his resignation.

stories.headline: Avi Lewis elected NDP federal leader on first ballot, faces immediate division from Prairie wings
stories.summary: Filmmaker and activist Avi Lewis won the NDP leadership with 56% of votes at the party's Winnipeg convention, succeeding Jagmeet Singh. Alberta NDP leader Naheed Nenshi and Saskatchewan leader Carla Beck immediately distanced their provincial parties from Lewis over his opposition to fossil fuel development, highlighting deep internal divisions.

stories.headline: Liberal MP Michael Ma faces calls for removal after questioning China forced labor expert
stories.summary: Liberal MP Michael Ma, who crossed the floor from the Conservatives, aggressively questioned witnesses about Uyghur forced labor in China at a parliamentary committee, appearing to downplay reports of human rights abuses. Conservative and other opposition MPs demanded his removal from Liberal caucus, while Energy Minister Hodgson suggested Ma's views don't reflect party positions.

stories.headline: Mark Carney's low Question Period attendance draws opposition criticism
stories.summary: Analysis shows Prime Minister Mark Carney has attended Question Period less than 30% of the time since taking office, significantly lower than his predecessors. Opposition parties criticized his absence from parliamentary duties while he travels internationally for trade and diplomatic meetings.

articles.title: As prime minister, Mark Carney makes Question Period a low priority

stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds interest rates steady amid Iran war inflation concerns
stories.summary: The Bank of Canada kept its policy rate at 2.25% amid concerns that rising energy prices from the Iran war could trigger broader inflation. Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers warned the central bank must guard against oil price increases spreading to other sectors, while financial markets bet on potential rate hikes later this year.

stories.headline: Carney's office clarifies he did raise human rights with Xi Jinping in Beijing meeting
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney's office corrected parliamentary documents that suggested he had not 'proactively' raised human rights or foreign interference during his January meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The clarification came after Conservative MPs questioned whether these issues were addressed during the Beijing visit.

articles.title: Carney-China: PM did raise human rights with Xi, feds say

stories.headline: Canadian Armed Forces members safe after missile intercepted near Israel-Lebanon border
stories.summary: All Canadian Armed Forces personnel in the Middle East were reported safe after a missile was intercepted near the Israel-Lebanon border. The Department of National Defence confirmed approximately 200 CAF members are stationed in the region, including UN Military Observers under Operation Jade.

stories.headline: Carney creates parallel bureaucracy structures to bypass federal civil service
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is establishing new parallel bureaucratic structures including the MPO (headed by Dawn Farrell) and Build Canada Homes (run by Ana Bailão) to work around what he views as an inefficient federal civil service. The strategy represents a workaround rather than wholesale public service reform.

articles.title: Mark Carney's strategy for the public service becomes clearer

stories.headline: Bloc Québécois activities across multiple Quebec and federal issues
stories.summary: The Bloc Québécois has been active on several fronts including criticizing federal language policy enforcement, supporting Quebec's secularism law at the Supreme Court, calling for employment insurance reform, and preparing for the Terrebonne by-election where candidate Nathalie Sinclair-Desgagné faces Liberal incumbent Tatiana Auguste.

stories.headline: RCMP and CSIS reviewing Vancouver company for alleged Hezbollah ties
stories.summary: Canada's national security agencies are investigating a Vancouver company that remains active in Canada despite being sanctioned by the United States for alleged ties to Hezbollah. CSIS confirmed that security agencies are 'looking at this issue and working with U.S.' counterparts on the matter.

articles.title: RCMP, CSIS reviewing Vancouver company accused of ties to Hezbollah, minister says
